t: Find Maximum Removals From Source String
o: Delete as many characters of source as possible, where each deleted index must be in targetIndices and pattern must remain a subsequence afterwards. Equivalently, choose a matching of pattern into source that avoids as many targetIndices positions as possible; the answer is |targetIndices| minus the minimum number of target positions any valid matching is forced to use. n ≤ 3000 invites an O(nm) DP.
k: DP over source position i and number of pattern chars matched j: dp[j] = max deletions so far; taking source[i] as pattern[j] gains 1 only if i is a target index.

Equivalently, index i (matching pattern char j) is deletable iff the prefix pattern[0..j-1] can match strictly before i AND pattern[j+1..] can match strictly after i — computable with earliest/latest greedy match arrays.
Both methods are O(nm) or better and exploit that pattern is guaranteed to be a subsequence.

a.i: Process source left to right; dp[j] is the maximum number of removable target indices used while matching the first j characters of pattern. Skipping a character is free; matching source[i] to pattern[j] adds 1 if i ∈ targetIndices.
s: For each i and each j (descending), if source[i]==pattern[j], dp[j+1] = max(dp[j+1], dp[j] + (i in targets))
a.t: O(nm) — each (i, j) pair is relaxed once
a.sp: O(m) for the rolling dp array

a.i: Index i carrying pattern char j is removable iff a full matching exists that avoids i. That holds exactly when the earliest match of pattern[0..j-1] ends before i (e[j] < i) and the latest match of pattern[j+1..] starts after i (l[j+1] > i), since prefix and suffix choices are independent.
s: Scan left to right recording e[j], the earliest end index of a match of pattern's first j chars
Scan right to left recording l[j], the latest start index of a match of pattern's last m-j chars
Count target indices i for which some j with pattern[j]==s[i] satisfies e[j] < i and l[j+1] > i
a.t: O(n + m + |targetIndices| · freq) — linear scans plus small per-index checks

w: The DP is the safest interview answer; the greedy is elegant but requires the independence argument to be stated carefully. Pitfall in the DP: iterating j descending so each source character is used at most once. Edge cases: pattern of length 1, target index 0 or n-1. Follow-up: report which indices to delete — keep parent pointers in the DP.
